name: Orforglipron
used_for: A once-daily oral, non-peptide small-molecule agonist of the GLP-1 receptor developed by Eli Lilly. The FDA approved it as Foundayo in April 2026 for weight reduction in adults with obesity, or with overweight and weight-related conditions, alongside a reduced-calorie diet and increased activity (per the current DailyMed label and trade press). It is not a peptide. Phase 3 trials showed weight loss and improved blood sugar control, with a gastrointestinal side effect profile typical of the GLP-1 class.

entries.text: Label: Foundayo (orforglipron) tablets, starting dosage is 0.8 mg orally once daily; after at least 30 days increase to 2.5 mg once daily, then after at least 30 days to 5.5 mg once daily.
entries.population: Adults with obesity, or overweight with at least one weight-related comorbidity, with a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity

entries.text: Label: Foundayo may be increased to the next level (9 mg, 14.5 mg or 17.2 mg once daily) after at least 30 days on the current dosage based on response and tolerability; the maximum is 17.2 mg once daily.
entries.population: Adults with obesity, or overweight with at least one weight-related comorbidity

entries.text: Label: Foundayo maximum dosage is 9 mg once daily when used with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor.
entries.population: Adults taking Foundayo with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor

administration_guidance.text: The Foundayo label states the tablet is taken orally once daily with or without food, and swallowed whole without breaking, crushing, or chewing.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: The Foundayo label states a missed dose is taken as soon as possible without doubling the next dose, and that after 7 or more consecutive missed doses the dose escalation is restarted at a lower dosage.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: The Foundayo label states tablets are stored at room temperature (20 to 25 C), with excursions permitted between 15 and 30 C.
administration_guidance.label: research

administration_guidance.text: An HCPLive podcast summary describes Foundayo as a GLP-1 pill for weight loss that can be taken at any time of day without food or water restrictions.
administration_guidance.label: internet

side_effects.text: The Foundayo label lists the most common adverse reactions as nausea (26 to 35% vs 10% with placebo), constipation (20 to 27% vs 9%), diarrhea (21 to 25% vs 11%), vomiting (13 to 24% vs 4%), dyspepsia (12 to 16% vs 4%), and abdominal pain (13 to 14% vs 7%).
side_effects.label: research

side_effects.text: The Foundayo label carries a boxed warning on thyroid C-cell tumors seen in rodents with GLP-1 receptor agonists (none were seen with orforglipron in rodents, and human relevance is undetermined) and is contraindicated with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN 2.
side_effects.label: research

side_effects.text: The label lists warnings for acute pancreatitis, severe gastrointestinal reactions, acute kidney injury from volume depletion, hypoglycemia with insulin or sulfonylureas, hypersensitivity, diabetic retinopathy complications, gallbladder disease, and delayed gastric emptying relevant to anesthesia.
side_effects.label: research

side_effects.text: In the ATTAIN-1 trial, treatment discontinuation due to gastrointestinal adverse events ranged from 5.3 to 10.3% across orforglipron groups vs 2.7% with placebo.
side_effects.label: research

internet_claims.claim: HCPLive hosts describe orforglipron as the first oral GLP-1 weight-loss pill without food or water restrictions, with about 12.4% mean weight loss vs 0.9% for placebo in the highest-dose group over 72 weeks.
A peptide-affiliate blog says orforglipron has no food or water restrictions unlike oral semaglutide; the page predates approval and carries affiliate links to sellers.

research.summary: FDA-approved DailyMed prescribing information for Foundayo (orforglipron) tablets, Eli Lilly, revised August 2026.
research.finding: Lists the approved indication for weight reduction in adults, administration with or without food, the boxed thyroid C-cell warning, and adverse reaction rates.

research.summary: Phase 3 randomized, placebo-controlled trial (ATTAIN-1) of once-daily orforglipron for 72 weeks in 3,127 adults with obesity without diabetes, plus lifestyle modification.
research.finding: Mean weight loss was 7.5 to 11.2% across the three orforglipron groups vs 2.1% with placebo; more than half of the highest-dose group lost at least 10%; adverse effects matched the GLP-1 class.

research.summary: Phase 3 randomized trial (ACHIEVE-1) of orforglipron vs placebo for 40 weeks in 559 adults with early type 2 diabetes managed with diet and exercise.
research.finding: All three orforglipron groups lowered HbA1c more than placebo (mean difference about 0.8 to 1.1 percentage points), reaching mean HbA1c of 6.5 to 6.7%.

research.summary: Registry record for ATTAIN-1, the phase 3 study of orforglipron in adults with obesity or overweight with weight-related comorbidities, with United States sites.
research.finding: Confirms the trial is registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (status active, not recruiting).

research.summary: Phase 2 randomized, double-blind trial of once-daily orforglipron (12, 24, 36 or 45 mg) vs placebo for 36 weeks in 272 adults with obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related condition, without diabetes (Wharton et al., N Engl J Med).
research.finding: Mean weight change at week 36 ranged from -9.4% to -14.7% with orforglipron vs -2.3% with placebo; stomach and bowel side effects led to stopping in 10 to 17% of participants across dose groups.

research.summary: Phase 3b randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (ATTAIN-MAINTAIN) for 52 weeks in 376 adults who had lost weight on injectable tirzepatide (205) or semaglutide (171) and were switched to once-daily orforglipron or placebo (Aronne et al., Nat Med).
research.finding: Among those whose weight had plateaued, orforglipron kept an estimated 74.7% (after tirzepatide) and 79.3% (after semaglutide) of prior weight loss vs 49.2% and 37.6% with placebo; the trial had no group staying on injections and lasted one year.

dose.summary: The label starts at 0.8 mg once daily and steps up at least every 30 days (2.5 mg, 5.5 mg, then 9, 14.5 or 17.2 mg), with a maximum of 17.2 mg and 9 mg if taken with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor, a type of drug that slows its breakdown. Trials used other doses (6 to 45 mg). Ro, a telehealth seller, repeats the label schedule.

mechanism.summary: It binds to and switches on the receptor for glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1), a gut hormone that helps control appetite. It is a small-molecule pill rather than a peptide. It lowers food intake, likely by reducing appetite, and slows stomach emptying.

items.text: The Foundayo label describes orforglipron as a GLP-1 receptor agonist that binds to and activates the human GLP-1 receptor. GLP-1 receptors are in brain regions that regulate appetite, and in animal studies orforglipron reached and activated neurons in those regions.
items.label: research

items.text: The label states Foundayo reduces body weight with greater fat mass loss than lean mass loss, decreases food intake (likely through lower appetite), and delays gastric emptying, with the delay largest after the first dose and shrinking over time.
items.label: research

best_documented_effect.summary: In the 72-week phase 3 ATTAIN-1 trial, weight fell 7.5 to 11.2% on orforglipron vs 2.1% on placebo. In early type 2 diabetes, blood sugar (HbA1c) fell about 0.8 to 1.1 points more than placebo.

items.text: ATTAIN-1 (3,127 adults with obesity, no diabetes): mean weight change at 72 weeks was -7.5%, -8.4% and -11.2% across the three orforglipron doses vs -2.1% with placebo; 54.6% of the highest-dose group lost at least 10%.
items.label: research

side_effect_groups.title: Common
side_effect_groups.summary: Mostly stomach and bowel effects: nausea (26 to 35% vs 10% on placebo), constipation, diarrhea, vomiting, indigestion and belly pain. Heart rate rose by 4 to 5 beats per minute on average, and hair loss was reported.

items.text: The Foundayo label lists the most common adverse reactions as nausea (26 to 35% vs 10% with placebo), constipation (20 to 27% vs 9%), diarrhea (21 to 25% vs 11%), vomiting (13 to 24% vs 4%), dyspepsia (12 to 16% vs 4%), and abdominal pain (13 to 14% vs 7%).
items.label: research

items.text: The label reports a mean heart rate increase of 4 to 5 beats per minute with Foundayo vs 0.5 with placebo, and tachycardia (fast heartbeat) in 3% vs 0.9%.
items.label: research

items.text: The label lists hair loss in 4 to 5% of Foundayo groups vs 2% with placebo, more often in women (7%) than in men (0.9%), and associated with weight loss.
items.label: research

side_effect_groups.title: Warnings
side_effect_groups.summary: Boxed warning for thyroid C-cell tumors seen with other drugs of this class in rodents, plus warnings for pancreatitis, kidney injury, gallbladder disease and others.

items.text: The Foundayo label carries a boxed warning on thyroid C-cell tumors seen in rodents with GLP-1 receptor agonists (none were seen with orforglipron in rodents, and human relevance is undetermined) and is contraindicated with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN 2.
items.label: research

items.text: The label lists warnings for acute pancreatitis, severe gastrointestinal reactions, acute kidney injury from volume depletion, hypoglycemia with insulin or sulfonylureas, hypersensitivity, diabetic retinopathy complications, gallbladder disease, and delayed gastric emptying relevant to anesthesia.
items.label: research

side_effect_groups.title: Low blood sugar
side_effect_groups.summary: Uncommon on its own (2% vs 0.2% on placebo in type 2 diabetes) but more common with a sulfonylurea (7%).

items.text: In a trial of adults with type 2 diabetes (Trial 2), the label reports hypoglycemia (blood sugar below 54 mg/dL) in 2% on orforglipron vs 0.2% on placebo, and in 7% of those also taking a sulfonylurea vs 0.5% of those not taking one. Insulin or sulfonylurea doses may need to be reduced.
items.label: research

side_effect_groups.title: In trials
side_effect_groups.summary: Stopping because of stomach and bowel effects was uncommon in the phase 3 trial and more common in a phase 2 trial.

items.text: In the ATTAIN-1 trial, treatment discontinuation due to gastrointestinal adverse events ranged from 5.3 to 10.3% across orforglipron groups vs 2.7% with placebo.
items.label: research

items.text: In a phase 2 trial, stomach and bowel side effects, mostly during dose increases, led to stopping orforglipron in 10 to 17% of participants across dose groups.
